analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence Morning Briefing (October 29, 2026)
key_insights: Pre-market futures are lower after mixed megacap tech earnings. GOOG is about -10% pre-market and MSFT is up. SPX is -0.3%, NDX -1.1% and RTY +0.5%, with Software down 3%.

The tape has a defensive bias with the AI theme being sold. Discretionary and Financials have a bid, which JPM reads as the broadening / ex-AI trade. That trade tends to move inversely to AI and megacap tech, and EU outperformance today fits it.

JPM calls the GOOG print a setback for the nascent re-ignition of the AI / tech trade. Given economic strength and a robust earnings cycle, it sees the broadening move possibly extending as it did earlier in the year.

MSFT: Azure beat buyside estimates by 1 point and operating income beat by 5%. Schilsky says the CFO needs to guide Q227 Azure growth of at least +48% Y/Y FXN at the high end so bulls can keep believing in +50% growth.

GOOGL: Schilsky calls the quarter a straight-up miss. Search missed buyside estimates by 2% even though query growth was the highest in 5 years, because pricing is declining more than investors thought. YouTube and Cloud revenue missed, though Cloud operating margin was strong. Consolidated operating income also missed.

KLAC (+3.3%) management views the 2027 setup as favorable and expects sequential growth for the next several quarters. Lead times average 12 months, memory inspection intensity is rising, and the company is tracking at or above the high end of its 2030 targets without calling that the new normal.

KLAC says China revenue should fall toward 27-29% of total in Q4 and into the low-20% range in 2027. Capex stays around 2-3% of revenue after a one-off India land purchase. Management would not guide to 2028 strength and commits only to KLA not being the bottleneck.

Fed Day: the October FOMC held rates on a 10-2 vote. Markets first reacted hawkishly, then reversed during the press conference. Chair Warsh said there will be no policy vote at one meeting in 2027 and two in 2028, which sold off the long end.

Warsh did not embrace the tightening bias implicit in the statement, was dismissive on household inflation expectations, and took comfort in financial conditions. JPM rates reads this as the Fed leaning on long-term rates to do its work, reducing the need for further hikes.

JPM rates keeps 10s/30s steepeners, which also benefit if Treasury keeps auction sizes steady next week. It also keeps 1Yx1Y zero-coupon inflation swap longs, arguing the rise in inflation pricing is persistent and in line with historical magnitudes.

JPM FX says the dollar sold off on the lower-frequency policy schedule and on inflation comments that were not as hawkish as they could have been. 2s30s twist-steepened through the meeting, which JPM treats as a useful dollar signal. The move is modest, and G10 currencies with real-asset links (NOK, AUD, CHF) are favored.

Market Intel calls the Fed outcome dovish despite growth running at an above-trend pace of about 5% real GDP per the last two flash PMIs. It suggests the Fed is focused on incremental tightening of financial conditions, mainly through credit markets.

Market Intel's stance is to buy tech / AI, plan for some broadening and hedge war risk with longs in crude and equity vol. It would buy dips, and sees the main risk as a kinetic escalation in the Middle East.
Iran has indicated it would likely target Saudi and UAE energy infrastructure while the SPR is at multi-decade lows. The worst case is escalation that hits Russian refining capacity again.

Midterms on Nov 3: some point to an AI sell-off in a Blue Wave. JPM is tracking polls against prediction-market odds in the Senate battleground states, and NYT now sees South Carolina as tied, Florida within the margin of error for the Dem candidate, and a 14-point Dem lead in Minnesota.

Earnings read-through on labor: ADP raised its fiscal 2027 pay-per-control outlook to about 1% from 0-1%, and layoffs are near multi-year lows. ODFL and CHRW are cutting headcount while volume grows, which suggests automation may weaken the link between business growth and labor demand.

Wage and benefit inflation persists. CHRW absorbs about $30 million of annual wage inflation, ODFL gave 3-3.5% raises and its fringe benefit cost rose to 42.8% of wages from 39.7%, and IP expects elevated energy costs to persist.

Consumer color is mixed. Leisure and hospitality is softening at ADP clients, healthcare is strong, Generac sees consumers trading down, and Lennox says elevated mortgage rates keep housing demand constrained.

AI infrastructure demand is accelerating. GEV's backlog rose from $176 billion to about $200 billion with almost $30 billion of new orders, and Vertiv's Q3 data-center orders rose more than 100% Y/Y organically, with the EMEA pipeline roughly doubling.

JPM launched a revamped Delta-One thematic suite with 50+ new baskets, 6 pillars and 10 years of quarterly rebalanced history. Two trade ideas are long US Holiday Spend (JPUXHOL) and a midterm pair of short Federal Gov Contractors ex Defense (JPUXFEDB) against long ACA Exchange Levered (JPUXACA).

US Market Intel view, published Oct 26: remain Tactically Bullish. The SPX lost 2.4% over two weeks with a shift to defensives, but growth at or above trend and positive earnings growth support stocks. About a quarter of the SPX has reported with no dip to pre-season forecasts.

Positioning has not fully washed out even though sentiment is in the Fear region, so the signal is less clear. Recession L/S and Stagflation L/S baskets both outperformed last week, which JPM calls curious given the growth data.

If Trump moves back to negotiation with Iran rather than kinetic action, JPM expects a broad rally led by tech and cyclicals ex-Energy. The monetization menu adds hedges via longs in oil / Energy equities and long vol.
Cross-asset: WTI -103bps at $101.72, Gold -104bps to $4,025, Silver -251bps to $52.63, 10Y at 4.993% and VIX at 17.10. Bond yields are lower by 2bp after Fed Day with the curve twisting steeper.

market_movers.rationale: Solid quarter with Azure beating buyside estimates by 1 point and operating income by 5%. The stock is up after hours, and the Q227 Azure growth guide is the next test.
Schilsky calls the print a straight-up miss. Search missed buyside by 2%, YouTube and Cloud revenue missed and consolidated operating income missed, with the stock down about 7% after hours.
Management sees a favorable 2027 setup with sequential growth for several quarters and is tracking at or above the high end of its 2030 targets. The stock is up 3.3%.

sector_views.rationale: Market Intel keeps buying tech / AI dips and keeps a preference for tech in the monetization menu, while planning for some broadening.
Constructive given consumer resilience and limited direct exposure to AI-related concerns (prior Oct 19 menu).
Longs in oil and Energy equities are suggested as a hedge against Middle East war risk.
Software is down 3% pre-market and is the main downside basket in Europe, as the AI theme is being sold.

earnings_insights: MSFT (reported 10/28 after the close): Azure beat buyside estimates by 1 point and operating income beat buyside by 5%. The stock is +5% after hours and +3.4% pre-market. Q227 Azure guide of at least +48% Y/Y FXN is the bar JPM names.

GOOGL (reported 10/28 after the close): Search missed buyside estimates by 2%, YouTube and Cloud revenue missed buyside, Cloud operating margin was strong, and consolidated operating income missed buyside. The stock is -7% after hours and GOOG is about -10% pre-market.

KLAC (reported 10/28): management expects sequential growth for the next several quarters, revenue growth of about 25%, incremental operating margin near the top of the 40-50% range, capex at 2-3% of revenue and China falling to 27-29% of revenue in Q4.
ADP (reported 10/28): fiscal Q1 pay-per-control growth of 2%, ahead of expectations. Fiscal 2027 outlook raised to about 1% from 0-1%.
GEV (reported 10/28): almost $30 billion of new orders in Q3, with backlog up from $176 billion to about $200 billion.
VRT (reported 10/28): Q3 data-center orders up more than 100% Y/Y organically, and the EMEA pipeline has approximately doubled Y/Y.
CHRW and ODFL (reported 10/28): CHRW average headcount down 10.4% Y/Y in Q3 and ODFL average headcount down 4% against a 2% decline in shipments per day.

Season-to-date: about a quarter of the SPX has reported with no dips to the pre-season forecast of about 13% revenue growth, about 30% EPS growth and about 15% margins. These are forecasts, not printed totals.
Today's reports: AMZN and INTC after the close, plus BMO names including CAT, LLY, MA, MRK, BMY, LIN and HSY, and AMC names including COIN, MSTR, SBUX, RBLX, RDDT and RIVN.

trade_ideas.rationale: The long end can steepen as the Fed gave up the tightening bias and the term premium is expected to rise further out the curve.
The rise in inflation pricing is persistent and in line with historical magnitudes.

trade_ideas.description: Buy tech / AI dips and hedge war risk with longs in crude and equity vol
trade_ideas.rationale: The primary risk is a spike in kinetic conflict in the Middle East, so JPM buys tech and plans for broadening while hedging.
trade_ideas.risk: Escalation in the Middle East and Russian refining capacity being hit.

trade_ideas.rationale: Spending is accelerating, seasonality is supportive and positioning remains under-owned.

trade_ideas.description: Midterm pair: short Federal Gov Contractors ex Defense (JPUXFEDB), long Affordable Care Act Exchange Levered (JPUXACA)
trade_ideas.rationale: Divided government means lower legislative productivity and more federal funding risk, while gridlock could put ACA subsidies back on the table.

risk_factors: Kinetic escalation in the Middle East, including Iranian strikes on Saudi and UAE energy infrastructure with the SPR at multi-decade lows.
Russian refining capacity being hit again.
Midterm outcome, with some pointing to an AI sell-off in a Blue Wave.
Further megacap tech earnings (AMZN, INTC) and the MSFT Q227 Azure guide.
Wage and healthcare cost inflation, and elevated energy costs.
Incomplete positioning washout despite Fear-region sentiment.
Tariffs, energy and AI uncertainty weigh on small business hiring.
vol_and_positioning: Market Intel suggests hedging war risk with long crude and long equity vol while staying bullish tech / AI.
Positioning has not seen a complete washout despite sentiment being firmly in the Fear region, so the buy signal is less clear.
In the JPM holiday spend idea, recent gains came from short covering rather than a broad rotation into long exposure, and positioning is described as under-owned.
Recession L/S (JPRECES) returned 3.4% and Stagflation L/S (JP9STAGP) returned 1.5% last week.
geopolitical: Trump says he is nearing a decision on Iran, negotiation or continued attacks, as a third aircraft carrier nears the region. Iran has said new bombing would bring strikes on the region, including Israel and the UAE.
Iran has indicated it would likely target Saudi and UAE energy infrastructure while the SPR is at multi-decade lows. The worst case is Russian refining capacity being hit again.
Nov 1: expiration of the one-year trade truce between Trump and Xi, with a note that the truce was agreed to be extended through January 20, 2027.
Nov 3 US midterm elections and a Dec 11 US government funding deadline are listed as political catalysts.
World Bank sees commodity prices up 23% in 2026 due to the Middle East war and other shocks.

tension_points.bull_case: MSFT delivered a solid quarter, KLAC sees a favorable 2027 and data-center demand is accelerating at GEV and VRT, so JPM would buy AI dips.
tension_points.bear_case: GOOG missed on search pricing, the AI theme is being sold pre-market and some expect an AI sell-off in a Blue Wave at the midterms, favoring broadening into ex-AI cyclicals.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A spike in kinetic conflict in the Middle East, which JPM names as the primary risk to the bullish view.

tension_points.bull_case: Warsh declined to embrace the tightening bias and took comfort in financial conditions, which supports steepeners and a softer dollar.
tension_points.bear_case: Growth is running near 5% with rising inflationary inputs, and the dovish press conference undermined inflation expectations, which JPM sees as persistent.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Upcoming Fedspeak, which kicks off on Friday, is the next cue that could change the dovish read.

tension_points.bear_case: A guide below the level bulls need would undercut the belief in +50% Azure growth.
